alt: The strict performance rule (Cutter v Powell; Re Moore and Landauer) above seven exceptions, each with its case: substantial performance, voluntary acceptance of part performance, divisible contracts, prevention, tender of performance, time of performance and vicarious performance.
caption: Exact performance is the rule; seven exceptions soften its harshness.

alt: Two flows. Actual breach: only a repudiatory breach (breach of a condition, a serious breach of an innominate term, or a refusal to perform) lets the innocent party choose to terminate and claim damages or affirm and continue. Anticipatory breach (Hochster v De la Tour; Frost v Knight): the innocent party may accept and sue at once, or affirm and wait, which is risky (Avery v Bowden); White and Carter v McGregor recovered the full price after affirming.
caption: Only a repudiatory breach allows termination, and the innocent party always chooses.

alt: Two columns. Types of frustrating event: impossibility (Taylor v Caldwell; Robinson v Davison; Condor v Baron Knights; Jackson v Union Marine), supervening illegality (Fibrosa) and performance made pointless (Krell v Henry, contrasted with Herne Bay v Hutton). Limitations: a contractual provision, mere inconvenience or expense (Davis Contractors; Tsakiroglou), foreseen or foreseeable events, and self-induced frustration (Maritime National Fish; The Super Servant Two).
caption: Frustration is narrow: a dearer or slower contract is not a frustrated one.

alt: Four steps in the law on money after frustration: Chandler v Webster left the loss where it fell; Fibrosa allowed recovery only on a total failure of consideration; the 1943 Act s1(2) makes money paid recoverable and money payable no longer due, with a discretionary allowance for expenses (Gamerco); s1(3) allows a just sum for a valuable non-money benefit (BP v Hunt).
caption: The 1943 Act replaced the harsh common law with recovery and a discretion over expenses.

alt: A bar to scale shows the £8,000 price split into the £2,000 deposit paid and the £6,000 balance, which ceases to be payable under s1(2). The deposit is then split into up to £700 kept for Marquee Masters’ expenses and £1,300 returned to Lena. Lena recovers between £1,300 and £2,000.
caption: Deposit back, balance cancelled, with up to £700 kept for expenses.
